newsitem.title: UK: UK stock outlook-Focus on UK data for rate clues.
newsitem.headline: UK stock outlook-Focus on UK data for rate clues.

text.p: Britain's FTSE 100 share index could see a bounce next week if investors get clear evidence the economy has begun to cool, strategists and dealers said on Friday.
The blue chip index, which had climbed to an all-time high at 5,095.3 on August 7, lost 3.3 percent on the week to end at 4,865.8.
"At 5,100, cash was looking a safer bet, but at these levels, I'll pick up the phone and advise clients to get back into stocks," said Robert Buckland, UK stock strategist with HSBC James Capel.
But any sign of economic strength will bring fears of an interest rate hike back into the fore and could pressure stocks further, strategists and dealers said.
"If growth is too strong year on year, it will raise the question again about whether rates have to go up," said Richard Jeffrey, head of research at Charterhouse Tilney.
With few companies due to report corporate results next week, next week's UK retail sales data for July and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting in the U.S. will likely be the focus.
"There are lingering worries that (UK) rates will have to go up again and (the BoE) left that door open," said one dealer.
The average estimate of economists surveyed by Reuters was a 5.4-percent rise in July retail sales on the year. Jeffrey said he was forecasting an increase closer to six-percent rise.
A higher-than-expected increase would likely drive shares lower and sterling higher, they said. A rebound in sterling could put pressure back on shares in companies with high overseas earnings.
Next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting is expected to result in no change in policy after a week's worth of data pointing to low inflation.

Other British economic reports due next week include July public sector borrowing requirement, second-quarter gross domestic product data, July money supply figures and the Confederation of British Industry survey.
The only FTSE 100 company scheduled to release results next week is Halifax.
Among second-liners, Argos, Weir Group and Bodycote International Plc are due to report earnings.
